overall_quality.evidence: Eventual consistency is a property of distributed systems where all nodes will eventually agree on the state of the system, but not necessarily in real-time. This means that after a write operation, it may take some time for all nodes to reflect the change, and during this period, reads from different nodes might return different values. The system guarantees that all nodes will eventually converge to the same state, but it does not guarantee that this will happen quickly or that all nodes will be in sync at any given moment.
